result.title: When Answer Decodability Is Not a Decision: Separating Final-Answer and Imminent-Emission Signals in Chain-of-Thought
result.summary: Answer probes applied to chain-of-thought hidden states are often read as evidence that a language model has already decided its final response. This reading overlooks a competing signal, the candidate the model is about to mention. We introduce emission-controlled dual-target probing (ECDP), which fits the same low-rank reader family separately to the imminent mention and to the final answer at identical positions, with target-specific nulls and thresholds fixed before any fit. On correct DecisionDepth (DD) rollouts in which a distractor is mentioned before the final answer, Qwen3.5-4B decodes the next mention at .966 (null .234) but the final answer only at .221 (null .186), an emission gap of .696 [.648, .744]; Llama-3.1-8B gives .575 [.514, .632]. This pattern is not universal. In a pre-specified evaluation of Qwen3-8B with thinking enabled on held-out MMLU questions, using a full-prefix attention reader over every thinking position, both targets are decodable and the final answer is read far more strongly (mention-minus-answer lift -.398 [-.459, -.336] at layer 22 over 467 questions). Model, task, positions, and reader change together between these settings, and an attempted matched comparison on DD produced no valid statistics because the imminent-mention probe did not train reliably, so we do not identify what reverses the order. On DD, planted-signal controls show that the reader recovers an injected final-answer signal at one tenth of full dose. Answer-candidate decodability is therefore target-relative and protocol-dependent: a strong answer readout does not by itself establish when a model commits, and a probe that fails to train is not evidence that the information is absent. ECDP is a practical control for distinguishing imminent text emission from evidence of a settled decision.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 emission-controlled dual-target probing（ECDP），在相同位置用同一低秩 reader 族分别探测「即将提及的候选」与「最终答案」，并配目标特定的 null 与预设阈值；在 DecisionDepth 上即将提及高度可解码而最终答案很弱，而在 Qwen3-8B thinking/MMLU 全前缀 reader 下顺序反转，据此主张答案可解码性是目标相对且依赖协议的。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文关于「答案可解码不等于已决策」的探针协议与 null、阈值、位置和 reader 设定，可供核查 LVR 中「内部状态是否真正承载并决定答案」的证据强度；其文本 CoT 结论迁移到多模态 latent 需另行验证。
